header: Problem 4 Determination of Chloride by the Volhard Method. ① Pipette 20.00 mL of 0.1 mol/L standard silver nitrate titrant into a 250 mL conical flask. Add 30 mL water, 5 mL nitric acid solution, and 2 mL saturated ferric ammonium sulfate solution. While shaking, titrate with standard potassium thiocyanate titrant until a pale brown-red color appears and persists for 1 min. Record the volume of standard potassium thiocyanate consumed: V_{1} = 19.88 mL. ② Weigh 0.10 g sodium chloride that has been ignited at 500 ℃ ~ 600 ℃ to constant mass, accurate to 0.1 mg. Dissolve it in approximately 40 mL water in a beaker and transfer to a 100 mL volumetric flask. Add 5 mL nitric acid solution (1+3), then add 25.00 mL of 0.1 mol/L standard silver nitrate solution while shaking vigorously. Dilute to the mark with water and mix. Let stand in the dark for 5 min, filter through rapid filter paper, and discard the first 10 mL of filtrate. Accurately pipette 50.00 mL filtrate into a 250 mL conical flask, add 2 mL of 1 mol/L ferric ammonium sulfate solution, and titrate with standard potassium thiocyanate while shaking until a pale brown-red color appears and persists for 1 min. Record V_{2} = 4.01 mL. ③ Measure 50 mL test solution into a 100 mL colorimetric tube and otherwise follow the same procedure as in ②. Record V_{3} = 2.98 mL.

subquestions.text_open: 4.1 Calculate the concentrations of the standard silver nitrate and potassium thiocyanate titrant solutions.
